chunks: Your God is one God; there is no god other than He, the compassionate, ever-merciful.

key_terms.الرَّحِيمُ: The Ever-Merciful (referring to God's specific mercy)
key_terms.الرَّحْمٰنُ: The Compassionate (referring to God's vast mercy)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the oneness of God and His mercy?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited as the 'Verse of Tawhid' in Shia exegesis, establishes the absolute unity of God while simultaneously affirming His dual attributes of mercy, reflecting the balance between divine majesty and benevolence. It serves as a foundational declaration for Shia theological discourse on Tawhid, distinguishing the singular essence of Allah from the multiplicity of creation. The emphasis on Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim highlights the accessibility of the Divine, encouraging believers to seek closeness through both awe and love.
